cards.name: DIC Color Guide
cards.summary: Legacy XML colour book (.acbl) of 1280 entries in CMYK, named like 'DIC 1s' (book id 3012). It is the older XML copy of the DIC Japanese spot colour guide. The live Illustrator menu walk did not list it, so it is not offered under Window > Swatch Libraries. The strip draws 400 cells sampled evenly from the 1280 entries (the renderer caps strips at 400): pale pink, peach, lilac and aqua tints at the top, then rows of mixed saturated reds, oranges, yellows, greens, teals, blues and purples, with bands of browns and olives, navy and pale yellows in between, ending in saturated reds, purples, greens and blues. (Thumbnail: a swatch strip drawn by script from the file's entries, not a shipped preview.)
use_for: reading the legacy DIC names and numbers
comparing the old CMYK values with the current DIC Color Guide book
avoid: picking from it in Illustrator: the menu does not list it; use Window > Swatch Libraries > Color Books > DIC Color Guide
assuming spot behaviour: the legacy file carries CMYK values
cards.applies_to: none in practice: a legacy colour-book file that the menu does not list; if it could be loaded it would offer named CMYK swatches for fills and strokes of paths, shapes and type
cards.how_to_apply: Not offered in the Swatch Libraries menu (the live menu walk did not find it), so there is no panel route; the file sits at <Illustrator 2026 install folder>/Presets/en_US/Swatches/Color Books/Legacy/DIC Color Guide.acbl. Use the current colour book of the same name from Window > Swatch Libraries > Color Books instead. No loader call was harvested.

equivalents.PS: Presets/Color Books/DIC Color Guide.acb#DIC Color Guide

verified.note: 400 sampled cells: pale tints on top, mixed saturated rows with bands of browns and olives, navy, pale yellows, ending in saturated reds, purples, greens and blues.

review.changes: strip draws 400 sampled cells, not 1280; the bottom rows are saturated reds, purples, greens and blues, not browns, navy and greys

cards.name: HKS E
cards.summary: Legacy XML colour book (.acbl) of 86 entries in CMYK, named like 'HKS 1 E' (book id 3008), the older XML copy of the HKS E book (continuous stationery). Drawn from the file's CMYK values read as 0-255 integers (Encoding="Int8"), the strip shows the book's range in order: pale and full yellows, oranges, reds and crimsons, magentas and violets, blues and cyans, greens and yellow-greens, ochres and browns, a black, a beige and a dark brown, then a closing row of greyish greens and olive greys. The live Illustrator menu walk did not list it, so it is not offered under Window > Swatch Libraries. (Thumbnail: a swatch strip drawn by script from the file's entries, not a shipped preview.)
use_for: reading the legacy HKS E names and numbers
comparing the old values with the current HKS E book
avoid: picking from it in Illustrator: the menu does not list it; use Window > Swatch Libraries > Color Books > HKS E
judging printed colour from the strip: it is the file's CMYK converted to screen RGB, not the HKS inks on paper; check against a printed HKS fan
new artwork: it is a legacy copy; use the current HKS book, whose values may differ
cards.applies_to: none in practice: a legacy colour-book file that the menu does not list; if it could be loaded it would offer named CMYK swatches for fills and strokes of paths, shapes and type
cards.how_to_apply: Not offered in the Swatch Libraries menu (the live menu walk did not find it), so there is no panel route; the file sits at <Illustrator 2026 install folder>/Presets/en_US/Swatches/Color Books/Legacy/HKS E.acbl. Use the current colour book of the same name from Window > Swatch Libraries > Color Books instead. No loader call was harvested.

verified.note: The re-drawn strip shows all 86 cells as an ordered HKS range from yellows through reds, blues and greens to browns, not the pure-primary blocks the card described; summary and avoid rewritten.

second_opinion.note: Harness check: the renderer now reads the legacy book's Encoding="Int8" values as 0-255 per channel (LIVE_CHAIN_REPORT renderer fix), the strip has 86 cells, one per entry, and its colours are graded hues rather than full-or-no-ink blocks, so the old text described the earlier mis-render, not the book.

previous.note: Only flat pure red, green, yellow, blue, cyan, magenta, black and white blocks: a mis-render (the file is Int8 0-255, drawn as 0-1 fractions), so the real look cannot be confirmed; card says so.

review.changes: cause of the bad strip stated exactly (Int8 values drawn as fractions) instead of a guess

cards.name: Arrow
cards.summary: Symbol 'Arrow' from Illustrator's 3D Symbols symbol library: an orange block arrow seen at an angle, its head at the left pointing down-left and a notched (swallowtail) end at the right, extruded in 3D with a bevelled front in two shades of orange and a dark orange-brown side. (Thumbnail: one instance placed from the library and fitted to 300 pt on white, applied by script; natural size about 68 x 46 pt; not a shipped preview.)
use_for: call-to-action arrows on infographics and web buttons
pointer for process or step graphics
avoid: flat or minimalist layouts: use a flat arrow from the Arrows library
changing colour freely: it is a multi-tone grouped artwork; break the link and recolour with Recolor Artwork
cards.applies_to: the artboard of an open document: placing it creates a symbol instance, a linked copy of the symbol definition that can be moved, scaled and rotated like any object; the symbol must exist in the target document (placing from the library copies it in)
cards.how_to_apply: Panel: Window > Symbol Libraries > 3D Symbols; click the symbol (it is added to the Symbols panel), then drag it onto the artboard or press Place Symbol Instance. Script: doc.symbolItems.add(doc.symbols.getByName("Arrow")) in a document that holds the symbol; to use it in another document: app.open("<Illustrator 2026 install folder>/Presets/en_US/Symbols/3D Symbols.ai"), place an instance there, item.duplicate(target.layers[0], ElementPlacement.PLACEATEND) (the symbol arrives in the target document), then close the library with SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES.

verified.note: Orange 3D block arrow seen at an angle, wide head at the left pointing down-left, notched tail at the right, darker orange-brown extruded sides.

review.changes: the arrow points left (down-left), with a notched tail at the right; it was described as pointing right

avoid: colour-led layouts: it is grey only
tiny sizes: the ripple bands blur together
cards.applies_to: the artboard of an open document: placing it creates a symbol instance, a linked copy of the symbol definition that can be moved, scaled and rotated like any object; the symbol must exist in the target document (placing from the library copies it in)
cards.how_to_apply: Panel: Window > Symbol Libraries > Arrows; click the symbol (it is added to the Symbols panel), then drag it onto the artboard or press Place Symbol Instance. Script: doc.symbolItems.add(doc.symbols.getByName("Arrow 14")) in a document that holds the symbol; to use it in another document: app.open("<Illustrator 2026 install folder>/Presets/en_US/Symbols/Arrows.ai"), place an instance there, item.duplicate(target.layers[0], ElementPlacement.PLACEATEND) (the symbol arrives in the target document), then close the library with SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES.

verified.note: House-shaped up arrow filled with grey concentric metallic ripple bands.

cards.name: Arrow 15
cards.summary: Symbol 'Arrow 15' from Illustrator's Arrows symbol library: a golden-yellow arrow pointing left with a single head and a forked (swallowtail) tail, filled with a white maze or key pattern cut into the shape. (Thumbnail: one instance placed from the library and fitted to 300 pt on white, applied by script; natural size about 87 x 62 pt; not a shipped preview.)
use_for: back and previous cues with a craft look
avoid: clean modern UI: the pattern is busy
small sizes: the white maze lines close up

cards.name: Arrow 16
cards.summary: Symbol 'Arrow 16' from Illustrator's Arrows symbol library: a solid brown arrow pointing up with rough, torn edges that look like cut paper or a rough brush. (Thumbnail: one instance placed from the library and fitted to 300 pt on white, applied by script; natural size about 62 x 45 pt; not a shipped preview.)
use_for: up and increase cues with a hand-made look
avoid: clean corporate layouts: the edges are rough
tiny sizes: the torn edge turns to noise
